entry.title: Modular Sensor System for Digital Measurement of Finger Mobility (FLEXI-TRACK)

media:group.media:title: Modular Sensor System for Digital Measurement of Finger Mobility (FLEXI-TRACK)
media:group.media:description:
FLEXI-TRACK represents the future of digital hand therapy – fast, precise, and patient-centered.
Hand injuries are among the most common consequences of workplace accidents – and precise follow-up care is crucial for successful rehabilitation. In particular, the regular measurement of finger mobility is a key process, but one that has often been time-consuming and manual.
The FLEXI-TRACK prototype was developed in collaboration with the Fraunhofer Institute for Materials and Beam Technology IWS and Sensorik Bayern as part of a research project.
FLEXI-TRACK is a modular, patient-specific sensor system for digitally recording finger mobility. Small sensor mounts attached directly to the fingers automatically measure joint angles and digitally document the values – precisely, objectively, and reproducibly.
Compared to traditional manual measurement, the system offers significant advantages: ❖ Simultaneous measurement of all fingers in a single session ❖ Time savings of over 20 minutes per measurement ❖ Greater objectivity and measurement accuracy ❖ Direct digital documentation for further use in therapy
This not only makes the clinical process more efficient but also frees up more time for what matters most: individualized treatment and counseling for patients.
The project demonstrates how applied research conducted by the Fraunhofer Institute for Materials and Beam Technology IWS, in collaboration with partners from academia and industry, translates innovative solutions directly into medical practice.
More Information: https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/industry-solutions/medical-engineering.html

entry.title: Bipolar Plates – Smart Manufacturing Solutions for Mass Production

media:group.media:title: Bipolar Plates – Smart Manufacturing Solutions for Mass Production
media:group.media:description:
The development of alternative drive systems is an important research focus in the mobility sector. In addition to battery-powered vehicles, fuel cell vehicles will contribute significantly to reducing CO2 emissions in the future. However, for the economic implementation of the technology it is necessary to transfer the conventional single-unit production to cost-efficient manufacturing processes suitable for mass production. In this context, the bipolar plate is a core component – and at the same time one of the fuel cell‘s cost drivers.
Significant cost-saving potentials are provided by the patented CONTIbip production as well as innovative, precision-fit and mass production processes for coating, forming, joining and cutting. The essential part of the process is the so-called pre-coating of stainless steel strip by means of PVD coating. This is followed by the forming process and laser welding of one or more formed strips. In addition to possible per¬formance improvements, the process focuses in particular on a drastic reduction in production costs.
More information: https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/centers/doc/hp2bpp.html

entry.title: Sustainable Laser Processing of Wood-Based Materials

media:group.media:title: Sustainable Laser Processing of Wood-Based Materials
media:group.media:description:
As a renewable and locally available material, wood contributes significantly to climate neutrality and sustainability. At the same time, the raw material base of the wood industry is shifting fundamentally. Central European conifer monocultures are giving way to mixed coniferous and deciduous forest stands, driving growing volumes of hardwood and damaged timber into the market. This is exactly where the Fraunhofer Institute for Material and Beam Technology IWS opens up new processing options through laser-based manufacturing. The technology delivers precise, reproducible, and localized material removal as well as targeted surface modification. Fraunhofer IWS develops these approaches for applications in timber construction, transportation, furniture manufacturing, and mechanical engineering, while combining precise laser processes with the requirements of industrial production. In this way, Fraunhofer IWS expands processing options for emerging wood resources.
Climate change, drought stress, pest infestation, and extreme weather events are accelerating this shift. The increasing anatomical and chemical heterogeneity of these resources challenges established processing methods. Hybrid construction methods add further complexity and increase the need for stable, flexible, and cost-efficient production processes. Laser processing meets these demands with high process speed, short machining times, and a contact-free process that avoids tool wear. This approach supports efficient, low-maintenance machining even for dense and abrasive hardwood materials. Stable process parameters ensure consistent quality and support seamless integration into automated inline production.
Laser finger jointing provides a particularly relevant example. The process offers an alternative to conventional milling for finger joints and relies on precise, localized material removal by laser irradiation. In the process shown here, the technology processes Robinia and beech by way of example. Finger joints play a key role in timber construction by creating durable, load-bearing connections between shorter wood segments and longer structural members. Laser finger jointing improves material utilization and supports uniform load transfer within the joint. High process flexibility allows different finger-joint geometries without changing tools. Mechanical milling, by contrast, requires dedicated tools for each geometry. Laser processing, therefore, enables the reliable industrial-scale production of load-bearing, dimensionally stable wood joints.

entry.title: Defektfreie und hochwertige ta-C-Schichten dank Plasmafilter und gezielter Partikelumlenkung

media:group.media:title: Defektfreie und hochwertige ta-C-Schichten dank Plasmafilter und gezielter Partikelumlenkung
media:group.media:description: Durch eine Umlenkung des Beschichtungsplasmas mittels elektrischer und magnetischer Felder gelingt eine Abtrennung der unvermeidlich mitverdampften Makropartikel und damit eine effektive Plasmafilterung. Ohne Filterung werden Makropartikel in die wachsende Schicht eingebaut, was zu einer rauen Oberfläche und einer hohen Defektdichte führt. Durch den Einsatz eines Plasmafilters entstehen hingegen nahezu defektfreie und glatte Schichten. Die so hergestellten ta-C-Schichten können ohne zusätzliche Nachglättung direkt eingesetzt werden – ein entscheidender Vorteil für industrielle Anwendungen mit höchsten Anforderungen an Oberflächenqualität und Verschleißschutz.

entry.title: DRYtraec® – Cost-efficient energy storage for the electric car of tomorrow

media:group.media:title: DRYtraec® – Cost-efficient energy storage for the electric car of tomorrow
media:group.media:description:
The demand for green technologies is growing immensely. More and more electric vehicles are hitting the roads, while the importance of electronic devices in people's lives continues to grow unabated. This brings the efficient and environmentally friendly production of battery cells into focus. For example, since the price of an electric vehicle is significantly influenced by the cost of the battery, economical and environmentally friendly manufacturing processes are the focus of the industry.
Fraunhofer IWS scientists developed DRYtraec®, a novel process that enables cost-efficient and environmentally friendly manufacturing of battery electrodes. The process completely eliminates the use of toxic solvents as well as the energy and cost intensive drying of the electrode layers. In addition to lithium-ion battery electrodes, the process can also be used to manufacture electrodes for novel cell technologies such as lithium-sulfur and solid-state batteries in high quality without the use of solvents.
More about DRYtraec® and Battery Technology at Fraunhofer IWS: https://www.drytraec.de/en.html https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/centers/abtc.html https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/technologyfields/battery-technology.html

entry.title: Unlock New Speeds in Thin Sheet Contour Cutting with EDcut

media:group.media:title: Unlock New Speeds in Thin Sheet Contour Cutting with EDcut
media:group.media:description: When it comes to contour cutting thin sheets (up to approx. 1.5 mm), traditional motion dynamics have limited the ability to boost processing speeds. That changes with EDcut — a next-generation development platform designed to break through these barriers. By merging cutting-edge system technology with laser process optimization, EDcut delivers a holistic performance leap. This innovative platform integrates high-speed motion dynamics with advanced fiber-guided solid-state lasers, enabling faster, more precise cutting than ever before. Whether you're exploring feasibility or developing custom technology solutions, the EDcut system is ready — engineered for innovation and built for results.

entry.title: PaPure – Additive-free Laser Joining of Paper

media:group.media:title: PaPure – Additive-free Laser Joining of Paper
media:group.media:description: The PaPure project's demonstration plant enables the production of packaging bags using innovative laser joining technology for the first time. Paper is continuously unwound from a roll, irradiated, and joined. This enables the production of square bags at a rate of 10 pieces per minute. The seal seam is continuously monitored by camera and the seam strength is automatically verified on a sample basis.

entry.title: Additive Manufacturing Capabilities for ATHENA Large Optical Bench

media:group.media:title: Additive Manufacturing Capabilities for ATHENA Large Optical Bench
media:group.media:description:
The large-scale scientific mission NewATHENA, run by the European Space Agency (ESA), will explore the hot and energetic universe using advanced X-ray technology. The key components of the telescope will be hundreds of Silicon Porous Optics (SPO) modules arranged in an optical bench with a diameter of around 2.7 meters. Considering the overall size, the delicate cellular structure and the high aspect ratio in combination with the material-related challenges of Ti6Al4V, Additive Manufacturing using Direct Energy Deposition (DED) is a promising alternative to conventional processing.
For more information about the project, please visit our website: https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/technologyfields/additive-manufacturing-and-surface-technologies/direct-energy-deposition-and-hybrid-manufacturing/newathena.html
Acknowledgements: The present work has been directly funded by ESA during the research activities “ATHENA” and “ATHENA Maturation” within the framework of the large class science space mission “NewATHENA”.

media:group.media:title: Extremely Dynamic Laser Cutting
media:group.media:description:
In the contour cutting of thin sheets (up to around 1.5 mm in thickness), the movement dynamics restrict the potential to increase process speed. The EDcut development platform now offers a solution to overcome these limitations. Along with advancing system technology, efforts are also focused on optimizing the cutting technology.
The primary focus is on a comprehensive approach that integrates both motion dynamics and the laser cutting process. The highly dynamic EDcut cutting system, combined with fiber-guided solid-state lasers, is available for feasibility studies as well as technology and system engineering developments.
For more information about the project, please visit our website: https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/technologyfields/cutting-and-joining/laser_cutting/system-development.html#fast-cutting
Copyright video: © Fraunhofer IWS

media:group.media:title: Simulation of Arc-PVD Coating Processes
media:group.media:description: Arc-PVD processes are hard to calculate because of the stochastic character of the arc spot motion. A semi empirical approach allows the simulation of the arc spot motion based on materials- and process data. So the target erosion profile is simulated and can be used for optimization of target utilization. On the other hand, spot behaviour is used to calculate the plasma propagation and the coating deposition profile. So an optimization of fixture design and chamber filling of industrial coating processes will be possible in the future.

entry.title: LAwave – Non-destructive Mechanical Testing of Coatings and Surfaces

media:group.media:title: LAwave – Non-destructive Mechanical Testing of Coatings and Surfaces
media:group.media:description:
LAwave technology allows fast and non-destructive access to mechanical properties of coatings and surfaces. The influence of pores, cracks and delamination, as well as structural and material changes, can be detected by measuring the effective Young’s modulus. Applications include thin film coatings (PVD, CVD, ALD), thick films (e.g. thermal spray, laser cladding), 3D printed metals, semiconductor polishing and many more. The method is based on the spectroscopy of laser-induced surface acoustic waves and is used in quality control and R&D. Fraunhofer IWS develops customized measurement systems for industry and academia.
More information: https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/technologyfields/pvd_nanotechnology/coating_characterization/lawave.html

media:group.media:title: Review: Laser Symposium & ISAM 2023
media:group.media:description:

entry.title: Laser Technology for a Lighter Future Flying

media:group.media:title: Laser Technology for a Lighter Future Flying
media:group.media:description:
More information on the topic: https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/newsandmedia/press_releases/2024/press-release_2024-05_CONTIjoin-ESL-BUSTI.html ___ CO2 laser system technology by Fraunhofer IWS enables efficient joining of large volume fiber composite aircraft structures:
Fraunhofer IWS has achieved decisive progress towards new ecological aircraft construction concepts. Within the EU programm Clean Sky 2 in the project “Multifunctional Fuselage Demonstrator” (MFFD), a team of researchers in Dresden provided proof of concept for the chipless joining of carbon fiber-reinforced thermoplastic component structures. The automated process approach developed joined the upper and lower halves of the world's largest CFRTP aircraft fuselage segment. In addition to saving on labor, for instance when drilling and riveting, the novel construction method and the CONTIjoin process enable massive reduction in weight, material and time. As a result, the production of future commercial aircraft should become faster, more eco-friendly and competitive. The researchers will present their results and the system technology at the International Aerospace Exhibition ILA 2024 in Berlin.

entry.title: Micro to Macro Using Highspeed Cameras – Technologies at Fraunhofer IWS

media:group.media:title: Micro to Macro Using Highspeed Cameras – Technologies at Fraunhofer IWS
media:group.media:description:
People understand their world with their eyes! Using high-speed imaging, you have your eye directly in your production process. For the efficient development of laser processes such as microstructuring, arc wire deposition spraying, welding, cladding, cutting or others, we use powerful high-speed camera technology with up to 300,000 images per second, various optics from the macro to the microscope range and special lighting that blocks out interfering process radiation.
More information: https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/technologyfields/cutting-and-joining/microprocessing.html

entry.title: Roll-to-roll Processing with Direct Laser Interference Patterning (DLIP)

media:group.media:title: Roll-to-roll Processing with Direct Laser Interference Patterning (DLIP)
media:group.media:description:
Direct Laser Interference Patterning (DLIP) is used to texture current collector foils in a roll-to-roll process using a high-power picosecond pulsed laser system operating at either 1064 nm or 532 nm. The laser beam is shaped into an elongated top-hat intensity profile and split into diffraction orders. The interference pattern is generated at the working position. Aluminum and copper foils of different thicknesses were processed. Composite electrode materials were coated onto the structured current collectors, resulting in increased specific discharge capacity for cathode materials, demonstrating the potential of DLIP for cost-effective battery cell production with enhanced cycle lifetime.
More Information: https://www.iws.fraunhofer.de/en/technologyfields/cutting-and-joining/direct-laser-interference-patterning/dlip.html
